title: rosa arvensis var. glandulosa
intro: Rosa arvensis var. glandulosa, commonly known as Wild Prairie Rose, is a variety of flowering plant in the rose family native to North America. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its numerous health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antioxidant properties, which can help to soothe skin irritations, reduce fever, and protect against cell damage. The bioactive constituents of Wild Prairie Rose include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory effects. The plant's therapeutic actions also include antioxidant, anti-cancer, and anti-diabetic properties, making it a valuable resource for natural medicine.
